target_customer: Real estate developers and investors in Germany needing commercial property financing
problem: Commercial real estate financing in Germany is fragmented and manual. hypcloud acted as a tech-enabled broker connecting borrowers with a network of lenders.
business_model: Commercial mortgage broker earning fees from financing placed

founders.name: Yann Basly
founders.background_notes: The YC page gives no bio. An aggregator lists him as CTO, not verified.

technical_complexity.rationale: A brokerage workflow and lender matching platform; the hard part was lender relationships and domain knowledge.

defensibility.rationale: Lender relationships help but the model was copyable by established platforms.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Hypoport announced a commercial property financing platform later; the exit was an acquisition by Wuest Partner reported in October 2025.

market_need_then: German commercial real estate lending is described in later coverage as fragmented with few standardised channels; no dated 2018 demand source was opened.

branding.domain_note: hypcloud.com now redirects to a domain sales page, so the company's own site is gone.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand was found and the invented name is hard to spell.

outcome_analysis: hypcloud was a Berlin commercial mortgage broker that joined YC in Summer 2018 and reached a team of 14. An aggregator reports that Wuest Partner acquired it in October 2025, but terms and rationale are not public and no press release was found, so the story is unclear and the outcome cannot be judged as strong or weak.
notes: Exit appears only on CB Insights, so date and acquirer are unverified; the status Acquired on the YC page agrees. Funding is aggregator only: CB Insights about 1.31M over six rounds, Seedtable a 120K pre-seed in August 2018 and a 2.7M seed in June 2019; unverified and not recorded as rounds. No dated competitor near 2018 was found (Hypoport's commercial platform plans are later), so the list is empty. Founder background not found. Completeness pass: both rounds rest on a single database (Seedtable); Welcome to the Jungle gives 2.7M seed in 2019-06 and 0.2M in 2018-09, Clera 2.5M total, CB Insights 1.31M over 6 rounds, so seed amount conflicts and is left null. Startbase lists other former managing directors but does not call them co-founders, so no founder was added.
